references.text: Parallel text describing the original instruction to make four bronze rings in the four corners of the grate for the altar of burnt offering.
The same construction principle with four rings cast into four corners, here for the ark of the covenant, which holds the carrying poles.
Similar construction where four gold rings are cast onto the four feet of the ark to hold the carrying poles.
Four gold rings are cast onto the four corners of the table of showbread as holders for the carrying poles, using the same construction method.
Direct follow-up describing how the carrying poles were inserted into the rings mentioned in verse 5.
Connects the making of the carrying support points (the rings) with their actual liturgical use (inserting the poles).
Creates a clear parallel between the bronze altar and the grate, as both are mobile bronze structures equipped with carrying poles.
Completes the description of mobility by showing what the rings from the source verse are actually meant to hold.
Extends the principle of mobility to apply to all holy furniture, not just those made of bronze.
Confirms the universal design logic in the tabernacle where all central furnishings are equipped for transport.
